answer: Trust propagates through an attestation graph by bounded-length random walks, so voting influence depends on reachable, independently vouched nodes rather than raw identities. A sybil cluster joined to honest nodes through a sparse inlet has low conductance; min-cut and transitivity bounds constrain the walk probability crossing that cut and, when weight is assigned by reachability, the cluster’s aggregate voting weight. A thread of mutually endorsing walnut accounts cannot evade the bound without external attestations.
